root_cause.text: The `dmemcg_limit_write` function fails to validate that the `options` pointer (the substring after the region name in the write input) is non-NULL before passing it to `strcmp`, causing a NULL pointer dereference when writing only a region name without any options (e.g., "test/region0").
root_cause.evidence: The crash trace shows `strcmp` at RIP with RDI=0x0 (NULL pointer). The patch adds a guard `if (!options || !*options) return -EINVAL;` after parsing the region name, directly addressing the missing validation. The CVE description confirms the trigger command is "echo test/region0 > dmem.max", which supplies only a region name without options.
